surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of NiCp2 and NH3 plasma on the Ni surface, leading to the formation of Ni-N and Ni-C bonds. The decomposition of the cyclepentadienyl ligand at higher temperatures produces more carbon free radicals, increasing the probability of bonding between C and Ni atoms. Post-annealing removes N and most of C, leading to a reduction in film thickness and an increase in metallic Ni content.
evidence: As indicated by Kim 15 et al., if the molecular structure of the precursor contains O atoms, for instance, Ni(dmamb)2 and Ni(iPr-DAD)2, this will pose a risk of oxygen incorporation into the ALD Ni film. Therefore, an oxygen-free metallorganic precursor could be much suitable for ALD Ni thin films. The decomposition of the cyclepentadienyl ligand at higher temperatures leads to more carbon free radicals. The Ni 2p3/2 envelop is separated into three components, which are located at 852.7 ± 0.1 eV, 853.5 ± 0.1 eV and 854.4 ± 0.1 eV, respectively. The strong peak at the smallest binding energy should be attributed to metallic Ni atoms (Ni0), which are dominant in the ALD film. The peak at the largest binding energy (i.e., 854.5 ± 0.1 eV) should be attributed to Ni-N, and the peak at 853.6± 0.1 eV is ascribed to Ni-C.
